title: Akshay Kumar Opens the Jungle. After 19 Years, 'Welcome' Returns With Half of Bollywood and a Plagiarism Debate.
excerpt: An absurd ensemble, 18 censor cuts, and a 'Tropic Thunder' comparison — 'Welcome To The Jungle' storms into theatres June 26 as advance booking opens.
body:
There's a particular kind of Bollywood chaos that only one franchise has ever bottled properly — the kind where Paresh Rawal is screaming, somebody's mistaken identity is about to detonate, and the body count of the gags is higher than the body count of the plot. After nineteen years and one wobbly sequel, Welcome is back. And this time it's gone full jungle.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=R704yP3dlXw

Welcome To The Jungle — the third instalment of the beloved comedy franchise, and unofficially "Welcome 3" — opens in theatres worldwide on June 26, with paid previews on the 25th and advance booking flinging open on Tuesday, three full days ahead of release. The early online interest is already loud. Trade projections are calling it one of the biggest Bollywood bets of the year, and one look at the cast list tells you why.

https://x.com/SacnilkEntmt/status/2068626101480681715

Director Ahmed Khan hasn't so much cast a film as staged a reunion of half the industry. Akshay Kumar headlines — returning to broad, unapologetic comedy at the exact moment his fans have been begging for it — alongside Suniel Shetty, Paresh Rawal, Arshad Warsi, Jacqueline Fernandez, Disha Patani, Raveena Tandon, Lara Dutta, Jackie Shroff, Johnny Lever, Rajpal Yadav, Tusshar Kapoor, Shreyas Talpade, Urvashi Rautela, Krushna Abhishek and more. It is, frankly, an absurd amount of star power crammed into one frame, and absurd excess has always been this franchise's entire point.

The trailer leaned into exactly that — a wall of familiar faces hurled into a jungle, mugging, screaming, slapping, double-crossing. It packs comedy, action and a heavy dose of nostalgia into two and a half minutes of organised mayhem. And it landed Akshay back where audiences have always loved him most: not saving the nation, not delivering a message, just being very funny in a very loud movie.

But the trailer also handed the internet a debate. Netizens were quick to note that the central premise — a group heading into a jungle to shoot a fake film, only to stumble into very real danger — bears more than a passing resemblance to the 2008 Hollywood satire Tropic Thunder, in which a cast of pampered actors shooting a war movie find themselves in an actual warzone. Sharper-eyed viewers pointed out it also echoes Akshay's own Tees Maar Khan, which similarly revolved around a fake shoot. The makers haven't addressed the comparisons. Whether it's homage, coincidence or a "masala remix" depends entirely on how charitable your Friday-night mood is — and this franchise has never once pretended originality was the assignment.

The road to release wasn't entirely smooth. The Central Board of Film Certification handed the film a U/A but only after reportedly asking for a hefty 18 modifications — among them the removal of a Kashmir-related dialogue reference, a toning-down of suggestive bikini visuals featuring Disha Patani and Jacqueline Fernandez, and trims to abusive language, double-meaning dialogues and some violent moments. After the cuts, the official theatrical runtime locked at roughly 2 hours and 45 minutes — making this one of the lengthier comedy entertainers in recent memory, and one of Akshay's longest films ever. That's a lot of jungle.

Ahmed Khan, reuniting with Akshay nearly two decades after their last collaboration, has been candid about the tonal trick he's attempting. "Watch it on mute and it looks serious," he said of the film's unexpected dramatic underbelly — a line that's either a clever tease or a warning, depending on how you feel about comedies that want to also make you feel things.

For the diaspora, this is prime Friday-night territory. Welcome To The Jungle gets a worldwide theatrical release on June 26 — expect wide screenings across the US, UK, Canada, Australia and the Gulf, the franchise's reliable overseas strongholds, where the Welcome brand of loud, family-friendly, leave-your-brain-at-the-door comedy has always travelled well. There's no OTT date yet; this one is built to be seen in a packed hall with an audience that laughs out loud.

It also walks straight into a box-office scrap. Cocktail 2 is still pulling crowds, and the two films will share the weekend's screens. But comedy and romance rarely cannibalise the same audience — and if there's one thing the Welcome franchise has proven across two decades, it's that Indian audiences will always, always show up for organised chaos with a familiar face at the centre of it.

Nineteen years in, the jungle is open. Whether it's a riot or a retread, the diaspora will be in line on Friday to find out.
